title: VSift time anchor v1
description: Time anchoring (0.3.0, ADR 0029): the time_anchor member of ingest and session status data, which says when the recording happened by the real-world clock and on what authority. It is present only when the session has an anchor; a session without one omits it, and every timestamped item then omits clock_time. An anchor ties one position of the timeline (media_time_us) to one clock reading from one source. The sources, in the order clock times are taken from them: operator (ingest --recorded-at, confidence exact), quicktime_creationdate (the recording app's own local-time tag, high) and container_creation_time (the container's UTC creation time, medium: many tools write the time they encoded or remuxed the file, and some devices the end of the recording). A file's modification time is never a source, and an online provider's upload date is not a recording time. consistency says whether the anchors agree: single (one anchor, or none that can be compared), consistent (every two that can be compared agree within two seconds) or conflicting (two disagree; clock times still come from the first source, and a reader should say they are disputed). Later releases may add sources (for example clocks visible on screen, at other positions of the timeline) and consistency values; a reader treats an unknown value as a reason to check the anchors list.

source.description: The anchor every clock time of the session comes from: the first of anchors.

recording_start.description: The clock time of the start of the timeline (media time 0) by the selected anchor.

anchors.description: Every anchor, in the order clock times are taken from them.

media_time_us.description: The timeline position, in microseconds, whose clock reading this is. 0 for every source of 0.3.0.

clock.description: One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere.

clock_time.description: The clock_time member of a timestamped item: the real-world clock time of the item's position on the timeline, from the session's selected anchor (see time_anchor in ingest and session status for whether the anchors agree). at is a point's time (a frame, a candidate's representative frame, an audio clip's first decoded sample); start and end are a range's ends (a transcript segment, a candidate's span, an audio clip's planned range). Absent members do not apply to the item. The whole member is absent when the session has no anchor.
